subject: Post-call recap: POC gates, KPIs, and next steps
messages:
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@datastream.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-03T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: POC gates, KPIs, and next steps

Hi Alex —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we have alignment heading into the trial: 

Summary of ask
- Datastream wants to validate a retrieval-augmented generation workflow for customer support summarization and suggested replies at scale. Primary constraints: low latency for agent-facing UI, predictable unit economics, and measurable lift vs. their current heuristic pipeline.

Proposed POC objectives (high level)
1) Latency & SLOs — maintain interactive experience for support agents
   - Target: p95 generation latency <= 150ms at steady-state (see load below)
2) Throughput — sustain realistic production pressure
   - Target: 200 requests/sec sustained with average output length ~80 tokens
3) Cost efficiency
   - Target: cost/token <= $0.0008 for inference (edge-to-edge) or clear quantization path to meet this number
4) Quality / relevance
   - Acceptance: human eval > 88% helpful/accurate on a 300-sample verification set; automated metrics (ROUGE-L >= 0.55) as a secondary check

Ownership & roles
- Datastream: Alex (product lead) and Priya (tech integration / sample workload)
- Redwood: Rachel (PM / trial owner), Ben (solutions engineer — runtime and benchmarks), Lauren (customer success — onboarding + eval cadence)

Deliverables we discussed
- Redwood provides a short POC SLO template and a pre-provisioned sandbox environment (shared network or API key)
- Datastream shares a representative sample workload (CSV or NDJSON), traffic profile, and a short README describing the hottest templates and expected token distribution
- Mutually agreed evaluation plan and scoring script for the human / automated checks

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Datastream: send sample workload + top 5 prompt templates by EOD Thu (Priya) — attachment welcome (we referenced datastream-sample-workload.csv)
2) Redwood: share POC SLO & runbook (attached redwood-poc-sla-template.pdf) and provision sandbox by Mon 8/6 (Ben)
3) Schedule 30-min kickoff to handoff to engineering (suggest Tue 8/7 10am PT) — Lauren to send calendar invite once dates confirmed

Open questions from the call
- Can Datastream accept a short cold-start period where p95 might be degraded during warm-up? We recommended a 10–15 minute warm-up window in the runbook.
- Which user journeys are highest priority (summaries vs. reply suggestions)? Knowing that will help Ben size batching / KV cache parameters.

Thanks — I’ll attach the template and share the Drive folder with the SOW draft.

—
Rachel Kim
Product Lead, Trials & Onboarding
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood-poc-sla-template.pdf
From: Alex Torres <alex.torres@datastream.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@datastream.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-03T17:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: POC gates, KPIs, and next steps

Thanks Rachel — this is exactly the kind of clarity we needed. Quick confirmations and notes from our side: 

- We can commit to sending a 1,000-row representative CSV with message + context by EOD Thursday. Priya will drop it into the Drive link you shared.
- Priorities: 1) suggested replies (high) 2) summaries (medium). Focus on replies for the first two weeks of the POC.
- Warm-up window: fine with the 10–15 minute warm-up as long as you record the window for the evaluation script.

Couple of asks: 
- Can Redwood provide a short script (Python) that emits load at the profile we discussed (burst to 250 rps, steady 200 rps, avg 80 tokens output) so our infra team can validate network and IAM settings?
- We’d like rough cost guidance for both hosted sandbox and a dedicated trial node (ballpark numbers are fine).

I’ve CC’d Priya — she’ll be our integration lead. We should have the sample file in the Drive by Thu.

—Alex
Alex Torres
Head of Product, Datastream
alex.torres@datastream.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@datastream.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@datastream.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2025-08-04T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: POC gates, KPIs, and next steps

Alex / team — quick technical checklist and what I’ll provision this week: 

What I’ll provision / deliver by Mon 8/6
- Sandbox API key + small dedicated instance group (GPU-backed) sized to handle 250 rps bursts and 200 rps steady with 80-token outputs.
- A small Python load generator that reproduces the traffic profile you described. I’ll include parameters (concurrency, inter-arrival distribution, token length) so you can tweak locally.
- Baseline run: I’ll run a 30-minute soak and attach a csv with latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99), tokens consumed, and estimated $/token using the default quantized profile.

Questions for Priya
1) Tokenization: are the messages already pre-tokenized or should we send raw text? If raw, we’ll instrument tokenization in the runbook.
2) Auth: do you want us to use mTLS or API-key over the VPN for the sandbox? Which would be easier for your infra team to accept?

Notes on acceptance thresholds (technical rationale)
- p95 <= 150ms is aggressive but achievable with small sequence lengths and batching tuned. If average output increases beyond 120 tokens we’ll re-evaluate the throughput target.
- Cost/token benchmark will depend on final model family and quantization; the sandbox will default to a mixed-precision profile so you can see a baseline.

I’ll attach the load script and baseline report to the Drive folder once complete.

Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com

Attachment planned: datastream-sample-workload.csv (please drop), load-generator.py
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Torres <alex.torres@datastream.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@datastream.ai>
Date: 2025-08-06T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: POC gates, KPIs, and next steps

Thanks all — scheduling note and proposed cadence: 

Kickoff: Tue 8/7 10:00am PT (30m) — agenda: scope, access, sample workload, and success checklist
Weekly check-ins: Thurs 30min (standup) with bi-weekly demo and alignment (owner: Lauren)
Evaluation plan (summary)
- Week 0 (8/7–8/13): integration + warm-up. Acceptance metrics recorded but not gated.
- Week 1 (8/14–8/20): baseline runs and first human eval on 300 samples (Datastream provides labels / crowd instructions). Goal: establish baseline quality and latency.
- Week 2 (8/21–8/27): optimization and model/quantization tuning; aim to meet p95 and cost targets. Final acceptance review on 8/28.

Acceptance checklist (final gate to consider POC successful)
- Functional: API calls succeed for 95% of calls during 1-hour soak at 200 rps (Ben to run)
- Latency: p95 <= 150ms during the 1-hour soak
- Throughput: no more than 5% request error rate at steady 200 rps
- Cost: measured cost/token <= $0.0008 using Redwood accounting for the chosen profile
- Quality: human eval >= 88% helpful/accurate on the agreed 300-sample set

Next actions (owners)
- Priya: upload sample workload + README by Thu 8/7 (Datastream)
- Ben: sandbox + load script + baseline report by Mon 8/11 (Redwood)
- Rachel: finalize SOW draft and share DocSend link by Mon 8/11 (Redwood)
- Lauren: calendar invites for kickoff and weekly standups (Redwood)

Looking forward — we’ll keep the check-ins tight so you get usable numbers for your internal stakeholders quickly.

—
Lauren Bishop
Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
